  stored.
- `dequantize_staging` -- Return the staged (w13, w2) shared experts,
  dequantized if needed.
- `finalize` -- Quantize the staged shared experts into the pre-quantized
  routed experts
- `load` -- Prepare the load of a fused shared expert tensor in
- `redirect_mapping` -- Point the expert params mapping of the shared
  experts to the staging
- `redirect_param_name` -- Parameter name a checkpoint tensor of expert
  expert_id loads into.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                          *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant*

TurboQuant: KV-cache quantization for vLLM.

Hadamard rotation + per-coordinate Lloyd-Max scalar quantization for keys,
uniform quantization for values.

The core algorithmic pattern implemented for key quantization (Hadamard
rotation followed by deterministic scalar quantization and re-normalization)
was originally established in DRIVE (Vargaftik et al., NeurIPS 2021) and
EDEN (Vargaftik et al., ICML 2022). This formulation is also mathematically
equivalent to the scalar case of the HIGGS quantization method (Malinovskii
et al., "Pushing the Limits of Large Language Model Quantization via the
Linearity Theorem", NAACL 2025; preprint arXiv:2411.17525), which
subsequently generalized these concepts.

A first application of this approach to KV-cache compression is in "Cache Me
If You Must: Adaptive Key-Value Quantization for Large Language Models"
(Shutova et al., ICML 2025; preprint arXiv:2501.19392). All of these
foundational and application references pre-date the TurboQuant paper
(Zandieh et al., ICLR 2026).

Modules: ~

- `centroids` -- Lloyd-Max optimal scalar quantizer for TurboQuant.
- `config` -- TurboQuant configuration.

Classes: ~

- `TurboQuantConfig` -- Configuration for TurboQuant KV-cache quantization.

         *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig*
`TurboQuantConfig` `dataclass`

Configuration for TurboQuant KV-cache quantization.

Applies Hadamard rotation followed by per-coordinate Lloyd-Max scalar
quantization for keys, and uniform quantization for values.

Historical note: the core algorithmic pattern implemented for key
quantization (Hadamard rotation followed by deterministic scalar
quantization and re-normalization) was originally established in DRIVE
(Vargaftik et al., NeurIPS 2021) and EDEN (Vargaftik et al., ICML 2022).
This formulation is also mathematically equivalent to the scalar case of the
HIGGS quantization method (Malinovskii et al., "Pushing the Limits of Large
Language Model Quantization via the Linearity Theorem", NAACL 2025; preprint
arXiv:2411.17525), which subsequently generalized these concepts.

A first application of this approach to KV-cache compression is in "Cache Me
If You Must: Adaptive Key-Value Quantization for Large Language Models"
(Shutova et al., ICML 2025; preprint arXiv:2501.19392). All of these
foundational and application references pre-date the TurboQuant paper
(Zandieh et al., ICLR 2026).

QJL is intentionally omitted: community consensus (5+ independent groups)
found it hurts attention quality by amplifying variance through softmax.

Named presets (use via --kv-cache-dtype): turboquant_k8v4: FP8 keys + 4-bit
values, 2.6x, +1.17% PPL turboquant_4bit_nc: 4-bit MSE keys + 4-bit values +
NC, 3.8x, +2.71% turboquant_k3v4_nc: 3-bit MSE keys + 4-bit values + NC,
~3.5x, +10.63% turboquant_3bit_nc: 3-bit MSE keys + 3-bit values + NC, 4.9x,
+20.59%

Parameters: ~

- `head_dim` (int, default: 128 ) -- Attention head dimension (e.g. 64, 96,
  128).
- `key_quant_bits` (int, default: 3 ) -- Bits for key quantization. 8 = FP8
  keys (no rotation/MSE). 3-4 = Lloyd-Max MSE quantized keys.
- `value_quant_bits` (int, default: 4 ) -- Bits per value dimension for
  uniform quantization. 3 = 8 levels, 4 = 16 levels (default).
- `norm_correction` (bool, default: False ) -- Re-normalize centroid vectors
  to unit norm before inverse rotation during dequant. Fixes
  quantization-induced norm distortion, improving PPL by ~0.8% at 4-bit.

Methods: ~

- `from_cache_dtype` -- Create config from a named preset.
- `get_boundary_skip_layers` -- Layer indices to skip TQ compression
  (boundary protection).

Attributes: ~

- `centroid_bits` (int) -- Bits for centroid generation --- always non-zero.
- `effective_value_quant_bits` (int) -- Actual bits used for value storage.
- `key_fp8` (bool) -- Whether keys are stored as FP8 --- no
  rotation/quantization needed.
- `key_mse_bits` (int) -- MSE bits actually used for key quantization (0 if
  FP8 keys).
- `key_packed_size` (int) -- Packed bytes for a single KEY vector.
- `mse_bits` (int) -- MSE quantizer bit-width (determines centroid count:
  2^mse_bits).
- `slot_size` (int) -- Total packed bytes per head per position (key + value
  combined).
- `slot_size_aligned` (int) -- Slot size rounded up to next even number.
- `value_packed_size` (int) -- Packed bytes for a single VALUE vector.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.centroid_bits*
`centroid_bits` `property`

Bits for centroid generation --- always non-zero.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.effective_value_quant_bits*
`effective_value_quant_bits` `property`

Actual bits used for value storage.

 *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.key_fp8*
`key_fp8` `property`

Whether keys are stored as FP8 --- no rotation/quantization needed.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.key_mse_bits*
`key_mse_bits` `property`

MSE bits actually used for key quantization (0 if FP8 keys).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.key_packed_size*
`key_packed_size` `property`

Packed bytes for a single KEY vector.

FP8 mode (key_quant_bits=8): head_dim bytes (1 byte per element, no
overhead).

  TQ mode: ~

  - vec_norm: 2 bytes (float16)

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.mse_bits*
`mse_bits` `property`

MSE quantizer bit-width (determines centroid count: 2^mse_bits).

For MSE key modes, equals key_quant_bits. For FP8 key mode, falls back to
value_quant_bits (centroids are still needed for continuation-prefill
dequant and decode kernel params).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.slot_size*
`slot_size` `property`

Total packed bytes per head per position (key + value combined).

Layout: [key_packed | value_packed]

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.slot_size_aligned*
`slot_size_aligned` `property`

Slot size rounded up to next even number.

Even-number is required so effective_head_size = slot_size_aligned // 2 is
integral.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.value_packed_size*
`value_packed_size` `property`

Packed bytes for a single VALUE vector.

Uniform quantization: ceil(head_dim * bits / 8) + 4 bytes (scale + zero
fp16).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.from_cache_dtype*
`from_cache_dtype(cache_dtype, head_dim)` `staticmethod`

Create config from a named preset.

Valid presets: turboquant_k8v4, turboquant_4bit_nc, etc.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.turboquant.TurboQuantConfig.get_boundary_skip_layers*
`get_boundary_skip_layers(model_config, n=2)` `staticmethod`

Layer indices to skip TQ compression (boundary protection).

For hybrid models (attention + Mamba/linear-attention), boundary protection
is disabled --- hybrids typically have only 8-12 full-attention layers and a
hard n=2 on each side would cover ~40 % of them. The dense GSM8K baselines
that motivate n=2 don't apply to hybrids.

For dense models, skips first N and last N attention layers. Empirically
required for aggressive presets (k3v4_nc, 3bit_nc) --- without it GSM8K
drops ~30 points on Qwen3-4B.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils._shuffle_deepseek_fp8_moe_weights*
`_shuffle_deepseek_fp8_moe_weights(w13, w2)`

Returns 4D weight tensors in BlockMajorK layout (E, K/block_k, Mn, block_k)

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils._shuffle_mxfp8_moe_weights*
`_shuffle_mxfp8_moe_weights(w13, w2, w13_scale, w2_scale, is_gated)`

Preprocess MXFP8 weights and scales for the FlashInfer TRT-LLM kernel.

All three transforms (gate/up row reorder, `shuffle_matrix_a` weight
shuffle, `shuffle_matrix_sf_a` scale shuffle) are fixed row/index
permutations that depend only on the per-expert matrix shape, so the
permutation is computed once and applied to every expert in a single gather
instead of once per expert. `block_scale_interleave` accepts a batched
`(E, M, K)` scale tensor directly. Output is bit-identical to the per-expert
loop but ~20x faster (a 288-expert MoE otherwise costs seconds per layer at
load).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.align_fp4_moe_weights_for_fi*
`align_fp4_moe_weights_for_fi(w13, w13_scale, w2, w2_scale, is_act_and_mul,
    min_alignment=16)`

Pad intermediate size so FlashInfer kernels' alignment constraints hold.

Some FlashInfer FP4 MoE kernels require the intermediate size used for GEMM
to be divisible by a small alignment value. When this is not satisfied (e.g.
with certain tensor-parallel sizes), we pad the gate/up and down projection
weights along the intermediate dim.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.align_moe_weights_for_fi*
`align_moe_weights_for_fi(w13, w2, is_act_and_mul, min_alignment=16)`

Pad intermediate size so FlashInfer kernels' alignment constraints hold.

Some FlashInfer MoE kernels require the (gated) intermediate size used for
GEMM to be divisible by a small alignment value. When this is not satisfied
(e.g. with certain tensor-parallel sizes), we pad the gate/up and down
projection weights along the intermediate dim.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm*
`align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm(w13, w2, w13_scale, w2_scale,
    is_act_and_mul, min_alignment, hidden_alignment)`

align_moe_weights_for_fi for MXFP8 weights and their UE8M0 block scales for
the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernel, which also pads the hidden size to a
multiple of hidden_alignment.

Padded weights are zero and padded scales are 127 (UE8M0 for 1.0), so the
padded rows and columns contribute nothing. Scales may be 3D [E, rows, cols]
or flattened [E, rows * cols]; their layout is kept. Returns the padded
intermediate and hidden sizes.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout*
`convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout(cache_permute_indices,
    w13_weight, w2_weight, is_gated_act_gemm=True)`

Convert expert weights to FlashInfer's block layout.

This reorders W13 and W2 in place into the expected epilogue-tiled block
layout and returns views of the shuffled weight tensors. Using one expert as
scratch space avoids allocating another full copy of both weights.

    w2_scale, w2_input_scale, is_trtllm=False)`

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_alignment*
`trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_alignment(per_token_activation, is_act_and_mul)`

Hidden-dim alignment for the TRTLLM-Gen NVFP4 MoE cubins.

The per-token (dynamic activation scale) non-gated variant has far fewer
tile configs for 256-aligned K and its heuristic default tactic fails with
"No valid config found" (e.g. Nemotron's 2688 -> 2816), so pad to 512.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils._upcast_e8m0_to_fp32*
`_upcast_e8m0_to_fp32(scale)`

Upcast E8M0 (exponent-only) scale to float32.

E8M0 stores only the 8-bit biased exponent (bias=127). To convert to float32
we place those 8 bits into the exponent field of an IEEE-754 float32 (bits
23-30) with sign=0 and mantissa=0.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton*
`silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton(input, group_size=128, output_q=None,

    expert_alignment=0)`

Fuse activation and FP8 quantization, optionally skipping expert padding.

`expert_ends` uses DeepGEMM's prefix-sum layout: each entry is the exclusive
end of an expert's live rows, including earlier alignment gaps. An expert
starts at the preceding end rounded up to `expert_alignment`. Padding
outputs are left unwritten and must not be consumed as live rows. Without
`expert_ends`, the original dense launch configuration is used and the
metadata loads are compiled out.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.gptq_utils.is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized*
`is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized(prefix, quantized_layers)`

Whether the routed experts at `prefix` are quantized in the checkpoint.

`prefix` is the absolute name of the fused expert layer (`...mlp.experts`),
while `modules_in_block_to_quantize` names the individual expert projections
(`...mlp.experts.0.down_proj`) or the fused expert module itself, using
either absolute or block-relative names. Match on the `experts` portion of
the name so that a layer whose experts are stored unquantized -- e.g. the
MTP layer of a partially quantized checkpoint -- is not given a quantized
method.

Configs that enumerate no expert module at all say nothing about the
experts, so the layer is assumed to be quantized.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                   *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils*

LUT-B weight format: 3-bit indices into per-tile E4M3 codebooks.

Rubin's `tcgen05.mma ... decompress::lut::b` instructions decode each weight
from a three-bit index into an eight-entry E4M3 codebook shared by eight
output channels. This module implements a calibration-free format matching
that contract. Each `8 (N) x 64 (K)` tile of a `[N, K]` weight stores 192
bytes of packed three-bit indices (row-major over the tile) and an
eight-entry E4M3 codebook. Separately, every output channel carries one
UE8M0 scale per 32 K (`[N, K / 32]`), which is exactly the hardware's
block32 B scale, so the 16 scales of a tile may differ. They keep
small-magnitude rows and blocks out of the E4M3 subnormal range. In total
the format uses 3.375 bits per weight.

Functions: ~

- `dequantize_lut_b` -- Reconstruct the [N, K] or [E, N, K] weight from
  LUT-B tiles.
- `lut_b_to_sm107_tiles` -- Rearrange stacked LUT-B weights into the SM107
  MoE kernel layout.
- `pack_lut_b_indices` -- Pack groups of eight 3-bit indices into three
  little-endian bytes.
- `quantize_lut_b` -- Quantize a [N, K] or stacked [E, N, K] weight to
  LUT-B.
- `unpack_lut_b_indices` -- Inverse of pack_lut_b_indices.

     *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._block_errors*
`_block_errors(blocks, exponent, tile_exponent, centers)`

Squared error of each K32 block, in units of the tile scale.

        *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._fit_tiles*
`_fit_tiles(values, weights, num_iterations)`

Fit one E4M3 codebook per row of `values` with weighted Lloyd iterations.

Three initializations are tried and the lowest-error fit per tile is kept.
Returns `(indices, centers, loss)`, where `loss` is the weighted squared
error per tile.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._normalize_centers*
`_normalize_centers(centers, preserve_zero)`

Snap to E4M3, keep an exact zero where needed, and sort.

    *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._refine_scales*
`_refine_scales(blocks, exponent, tile_exponent, centers, num_rounds)`

Coordinate descent over block exponents and the tile codebook.

Each round moves every block exponent by -1, 0 or +1, whichever decodes that
block best with the current codebook, then refits the codebook for the new
exponents. Each step is kept only where it lowers the error.

          *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._rescale*
`_rescale(blocks, exponent, tile_exponent)`

Per-tile values divided by their block scales, and Lloyd weights.

Each value is weighed by its scale squared, relative to the tile scale, so a
codebook fit minimizes the error of the rescaled weights.

   *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._ue8m0_exponent*
`_ue8m0_exponent(amax)`

Power of two that puts `amax` in (E4M3_MAX / 2, E4M3_MAX], as MXFP8.

  *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.dequantize_lut_b*
`dequantize_lut_b(packed, codebooks, scales, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)`

Reconstruct the `[N, K]` or `[E, N, K]` weight from LUT-B tiles.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.lut_b_to_sm107_tiles*
`lut_b_to_sm107_tiles(packed, codebooks, scales)`

Rearrange stacked LUT-B weights into the SM107 MoE kernel layout.

Returns `[E, N / 128, K / 128, 7168]` uint8. Each tile holds:

- 6144 bytes of 3-bit indices, 48 bytes (K128) per output channel, in the
  no-swizzle K-major core-matrix layout (8 rows x 16 bytes),
- 512 bytes of UE8M0 B scales: byte `q` of word `[lane][col]` is the scale
  of channel `col * 32 + lane` for K32 block `q`,
- 512 bytes of codebooks: lane `g` holds the two eight-entry books (one per
  K64 half) of channel group `g`; lanes 16-31 are zero padding.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.pack_lut_b_indices*
`pack_lut_b_indices(indices)`

Pack groups of eight 3-bit indices into three little-endian bytes.

    *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.quantize_lut_b*
`quantize_lut_b(weight, *, num_iterations=LUT_B_LLOYD_ITERATIONS,
    num_scale_rounds=LUT_B_SCALE_ROUNDS,
    max_tiles_per_chunk=LUT_B_MAX_TILES_PER_CHUNK)`

Quantize a `[N, K]` or stacked `[E, N, K]` weight to LUT-B.

Returns `(packed, codebooks, scales)` with shapes `[E, N/8, K/64, 192]`
(uint8), `[E, N/8, K/64, 8]` (float8_e4m3fn) and `[E, N, K/32]` (uint8
UE8M0). The expert dim is dropped for 2D inputs.

Each tile is fitted twice: once with its 16 block scales tied to one
exponent for the whole tile, and once with each block's exponent taken from
its own amax. Starting from the better fit, `num_scale_rounds` rounds of
coordinate descent then adjust the block exponents and the codebook
together. Every step only lowers the reconstruction error, so the result is
never worse than a single scale per tile.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.unpack_lut_b_indices*
`unpack_lut_b_indices(packed)`

Inverse of `pack_lut_b_indices`.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.check_moe_marlin_supports_config*
`check_moe_marlin_supports_config(config, group_size,
    allow_tile_padding=False)`

Whether the fused MoE Marlin kernel supports `config`.

With `allow_tile_padding=True`, a tile-misaligned intermediate size is
zero-padded to a valid thread tile at weight prep (see
marlin_moe_padded_intermediate), so only a group straddling the padded
boundary stays unsupported. hidden_size is the MoE I/O extent and is never
padded.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.marlin_moe_padded_intermediate*
`marlin_moe_padded_intermediate(intermediate_size, group_size=-1)`

Smallest MoE intermediate size satisfying the Marlin MoE thread tiles.

The kernel needs gate-up `2 * intermediate % 128 == 0` and down
`intermediate % 64 == 0`, i.e. `intermediate % 64 == 0`. A misaligned size
is zero-padded to the next valid tile at weight prep, kept a multiple of
`group_size` so the group count stays integral. The padded region never
reaches the MoE output: w13's padded output channels are zeroed by the
zero-padded scales, so the padded inputs to w2 are zero.

 *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.marlin_padded_nk*
`marlin_padded_nk(size_n, size_k, group_size=-1)`

Minimal (padded_n, padded_k) satisfying a Marlin thread-tile family.

Marlin GEMM and repack require (n % 64, k % 128) or (n % 128, k % 64);
shapes satisfying neither are zero-padded up to the cheaper family. K stays
divisible by group_size so padded scales keep an integral group count.
Padded weight regions contribute nothing to the GEMM output: quantized value
0 decodes to 0.0 (FP4/FP8) or is cancelled by the zero-padded
scales/zero-points (INT).

any tile padding) from its packed shape.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils_fp4.nvfp4_marlin_process_scales*
`nvfp4_marlin_process_scales(marlin_scales, scale_factor=None,
    a_dtype=None)`

Process NVFP4 weight scales into the special S0E5M3 format for Marlin.

Parameters: ~

- `marlin_scales` (Tensor) -- Weight scales tensor in half precision,
  already permuted for the Marlin kernel layout.
- `scale_factor` (float | None, default: None ) -- Optional power-of-2
  rescaling factor. If None, the factor is computed automatically so that
  every non-zero scale satisfies scale * 2^7 >= 2 (i.e., the MSB of the
  S0E5M3 representation is always 1). When provided (e.g., for MoE layers
  where all experts must share the same factor), the given value is used
  directly. The caller is responsible for dividing global_scale by the
  returned scale_factor to preserve numerical correctness.
- `a_dtype` (dtype | None, default: None ) -- dtype of the activations the
  scales will be used with. None keeps the dtype of marlin_scales.

Returns: ~

- `tuple[Tensor, float]` -- A tuple of (processed_scales, scale_factor).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils.mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz*
`mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz(w, scale)`

Reinterpret MXFP8 e4m3fn weights as e4m3fnuz without changing values.

The same bits read as fnuz are worth half, so each E8M0 exponent goes up by
one. 0x80 is -0 in fn but NaN in fnuz, so it becomes 0. The weight is
updated in place. Exponents 254 and 255 cannot be bumped and become 0xFF
(NaN); real checkpoints never use them.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils.requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0*
`requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0(weight, scale)`

Requantize block-FP8 weights to E4M3 with one UE8M0 scale per 1x32.

The SM100 MegaMoE feeds its scales to the block-scaled MMA, so they have to
be powers of two, one per row and 32 columns. A checkpoint with float32
scales per block (e.g. 128x128) is rounded once more to get there.

Parameters: ~

- `weight` (Tensor) -- (n, mn, k) E4M3 values.
- `scale` (Tensor) -- (n, mn / block_m, k / block_k) float32 dequantization
  scales (real = weight * scale).

Returns: ~

- `Tensor` -- (weight, sf): the requantized E4M3 weights and their UE8M0
  scale
- `Tensor` -- bytes, (n, mn, k / 32) uint8.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._e2m1_inline*
`_e2m1_inline(nibble)`

Decode an NVFP4 nibble (4 bits: 1 sign + 3 magnitude) to float32.

Uses direct IEEE 754 bit construction. For magnitudes 2-7 the FP32 bit
pattern is 0x3F000000 + (mag << 22), which is a single shift + add +
bitcast. Magnitudes 0 (zero) and 1 (E2M1 subnormal = 0.5) are patched with
two tl.where ops.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._e4m3_inline*
`_e4m3_inline(byte)`

Decode an FP8 E4M3FN byte to float32 without an FP8 pointer type.

Typed FP8 loads need SM89+ in Triton; reading the scale as uint8 and
decoding here keeps the caller portable.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._nvfp4_gathered_bias_kernel*
`_nvfp4_gathered_bias_kernel(markov_ptr, packed_weight_ptr,
    weight_scale_ptr, global_scale_ptr, values_ptr, index_ptr, logits_ptr,
    stride_markov_b, stride_markov_k, stride_weight_v, stride_weight_k,
    stride_scale_v, stride_scale_k, stride_values_b, stride_values_j,
    stride_index_b, stride_index_j, stride_logits_b, stride_logits_v, alpha,
    TOPK, K, NUM_BLOCKS)`

Apply selected NVFP4 Markov-projection rows to dense logits.

BF16: `weight[index] -> baddbmm_ -> scatter_`. NVFP4:
`gather packed W2 row -> dequantize 16-element blocks -> dot with Markov embedding -> add base value -> scatter corrected logit`.

The fused NVFP4 path is needed because packed weights cannot be indexed as
BF16 rows, while dequantizing the full vocabulary would defeat top-k.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._nvfp4_quant_dequant_kernel*
`_nvfp4_quant_dequant_kernel(input_ptr, output_ptr, global_scale_ptr, k,
    num_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, FP4_MAX_RECIPROCAL, TILE_BLOCKS)`

Fused NVFP4 quantize-dequantize kernel.

Uses a 2D grid (rows x tiles) to parallelize across both rows and
quantization groups within a row. Each program handles TILE_BLOCKS groups at
once using vectorized 2D operations.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._round_to_fp4*
`_round_to_fp4(x)`

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._triton_dequantize_nvfp4*
`_triton_dequantize_nvfp4(tensor_fp4, tensor_sf, global_scale, dtype,
    block_size=16)`

Dequantize NVFP4 using Triton (swizzle=False only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                  *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.ocp_mx_utils*

Functions: ~

- `ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows` -- Normalize a Quark weight quant config to
  (mx_dtype, scale_block_rows).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.ocp_mx_utils.ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows*
`ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows(weight_quant)`

Normalize a Quark weight quant config to `(mx_dtype, scale_block_rows)`.

Quark spells OCP MX weights two ways. The canonical one is 1-D per-group:
`qscheme="per_group"`, `group_size=32`, `scale_format="e8m0"`. MXFP8
checkpoints may instead use a 2-D per-block spelling (`qscheme="per_block"`,
`block_size=[R, 32]`, `scale_type="float8_e8m0fnu"`), which carries one
scale per `R` weight rows rather than one per row. `scale_block_rows` is
that `R`; it is 1 for the canonical spelling, where the two layouts
coincide.

Returns `None` when the config is not an OCP MX weight quantization.

            *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.SparseAttnIndexer*
`SparseAttnIndexer`

Bases: `CustomOp`

Sparse Attention Indexer Custom Op Layer. This layer is extracted as a
separate custom op since it involves heavy custom kernels like `mqa_logits`,
`paged_mqa_logits` and `top_k_per_row`, etc. Those kernels maybe requires
specific memory layout or implementation for different hardware backends to
achieve optimal performance.

For now, the default native path will use CUDA backend path. Other platform
may requires add the corresponding Custom Op name `sparse_attn_indexer` to
`custom_ops` in `CompilationConfig` to enable the platform specific path.

Methods: ~

- `forward_cpu` -- CPU sparse attention indexer: cache write stays eager
  Python glue

*vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.SparseAttnIndexer.forward_cpu*
`forward_cpu(hidden_states, q_quant, k, weights)`

CPU sparse attention indexer: cache write stays eager Python glue (own
K-cache layout, not shared with the main attention cache write). PREFILL and
DECODE both call the ported
`fp8_paged_mqa_logits_cpu`/`topk_transform_512_cpu` kernels, which read the
paged K-cache directly via `page_table` -- no eager gather step, no
per-request Python loop.

`prefill_metadata.chunks` always has exactly one entry here:
`DeepseekV4CPUIndexerMetadataBuilder` overrides the base chunk split to
always return the whole step's prefill batch as one chunk, since the base
chunking only bounds CUDA/XPU's dense M*N logits tensor and flat K-gather
workspace, neither of which this paged kernel allocates.

         *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._decode_chunk_ranges*
`_decode_chunk_ranges(rows, width, budget, itemsize)`

Partition independent Q rows under a payload budget of logits whose elements
take `itemsize` bytes.

     *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._gather_workspace_shapes*
`_gather_workspace_shapes(total_seq_lens, head_dim, fp8_dtype,
    use_fp4_cache)`

Return ((values_shape, values_dtype), (scales_shape, scales_dtype)) for the
K-gather workspace. FP8 path: (T, head_dim) fp8 + (T, 4) uint8 fp32 scales.
MXFP4 path: (T, head_dim // 2) uint8 packed mxfp4 + (T, head_dim //
MXFP4_BLOCK_SIZE) uint8 ue8m0 scales.

       *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._merge_dcp_topk_global*
`_merge_dcp_topk_global(logits, topk_indices, topk_tokens, dcp_rank,
    dcp_world_size, cp_interleave, row_starts=None, logits_dtype=torch.float32,
    num_positions=None, direct_max_rows=0)`

Merge each DCP rank's local top-K into the global top-K.

`topk_indices` are this rank's local top-K positions into its 1/N KV shard.
A token in the global top-K must also be in its owning rank's local top-K
(at most `topk_tokens - 1` tokens rank globally above it, hence at most that
many on its own rank), so exchanging only the per-rank local candidates is
exact -- equivalent to all-gathering the full logit matrix, but it ships
`dcp_world_size * topk_tokens` candidates instead of the whole score row.
Overwrites `topk_indices` with global token ids (`-1` for padding); the
attention backend localizes them back to physical slots per rank. The
selector keys only the score bits that `logits_dtype` (the dtype the MQA
logits were computed in, before the FP32 upcast) carries and the id bits
that positions below `num_positions` use.

Batches of at most `direct_max_rows` rows exchange the candidates over
symmetric memory instead of an NCCL all-gather (the workspace was created by
`SparseAttnIndexer`).

          *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._varlen_decode_rows*
`_varlen_decode_rows(q, q_scale, weights, kv_cache, decode, max_model_len,
    max_seq_len, topk_backend, topk_tokens, topk_indices_buffer,
    candidate_blocks, candidate_block_size, candidate_write, logits_dtype,
    start, end)`

The varlen (SM100) decode logits, candidate selection and top-k of rows
`[start, end)`, with the slice's own DeepGEMM schedule.

               *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.as_fp32_logits*
`as_fp32_logits(logits, row_ends)`

Upcast BF16 MQA logits for the FP32 top-k kernels.

Only columns below `row_ends` (int32, one per row) are converted, the span
the consumers read; DeepGEMM's aligned row stride is kept, with storage for
whole rows (gvr_2 reads the logits as [rows, stride]).

           *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.dcp_gather_kv_rows*
`dcp_gather_kv_rows(local_padded, deinterleave_idx, gathered_buf, out_buf)`

 *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.fuse_indexer_wk_weights_proj*

 *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.init_indexer_wk_weights_proj*

Build the indexer's checkpoint layers `wk` (BF16, or FP8 as the checkpoint
stores it and run in BF16: `bf16_linear`) and `weights_proj` (BF16), and
`wk_weights_proj`, the BF16 linear that runs both as one GEMM. Its weight is
not a parameter: it holds `wk` and `weights_proj`'s rows and is refilled
after every load and every in-place reload of the runtime weights
(`fuse_indexer_wk_weights_proj` from the indexer's post-load hook).

       *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.kv_cache_as_quant_view*
`kv_cache_as_quant_view(kv_cache, head_dim, use_fp4_cache)`

4D `[num_blocks, block_size, 1, head_width]` view expected by DeepGEMM, from
the 3D indexer kv-cache allocation.

  *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.should_skip_indexer_scoring*
`should_skip_indexer_scoring(mla_metadata, cudagraph_runtime_mode)`

Whether the indexer can skip scoring because the main MLA runs a pure
prefill on dense MHA, which does not read the top-k indices.

The indexer and main MLA may classify the same short extend differently
because they use independent decode thresholds, so this takes the main MLA
metadata. The indexer K cache must still be written.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                               *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_mqa_indexer*

Sparse Attention Indexer that scores only the candidate blocks.

DeepSeek V4.1 two-level selection: the candidate-source indexer publishes
the top candidate blocks and later indexers pick their top-k inside them.
`SparseAttnIndexer` does that by computing dense logits over the whole
context and masking; this layer instead calls DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits
kernels on the candidate blocks only, so the work is O(candidate blocks)
instead of O(context). It requires the `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`
metadata (see `AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits`).

Classes: ~

- `SparseMQAIndexer` -- Candidate-consuming indexer on DeepGEMM's sparse
  MQA-logits kernels.

                        *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils._amd_l3_cache_bytes*
`_amd_l3_cache_bytes(cache_info=None)`

The GPU's L3 (memory-side) cache size in bytes, or None.

The skinny-GEMM weight cap tracks this cache: past it a weight cannot stay
resident, and the skinny kernel's cost at n activation rows (~n weight
passes) pays HBM round trips instead. The device-properties API exposes only
the far smaller L2 (4 MiB on gfx950), so query the L3 through AMD's amdsmi
library: 256 MiB on MI355X, 128 MiB on MI300X-class parts. `cache_info` (an
amdsmi cache list) lets tests drive the parse; the default queries the
library.

                   *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils._bf16_mm_shape_supported*
`_bf16_mm_shape_supported(x, weight, bias)`

Shape and layout constraints shared by every FlashInfer BF16 mm backend.

              *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils._skinny_gemm_max_weight_bytes*
`_skinny_gemm_max_weight_bytes()` `cached`

Effective skinny-GEMM weight cap in bytes, evaluated once.

VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES > 0 overrides; 0 (the default) derives the
cap from the hardware L3 (memory-side) cache size, falling back to
_SKINNY_GEMM_FALLBACK_WEIGHT_BYTES where that cannot be read.
lmhead_skinny_guard_permits runs per decode step, so this is computed on the
first call only (env access in hot paths: #17067). Tests that change the env
var or mock the hardware read must call cache_clear().

                *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.lmhead_skinny_guard_permits*
`lmhead_skinny_guard_permits(weight, n)`

Should this weight still take the wvSplitK skinny path at n?

wvSplitK_hf_sml's cost at n activation rows scales as ~n passes over the
weight (MI355X measurements in the PR description), so past the last-level
(memory-side) cache its effective bandwidth collapses: every pass beyond the
first is an HBM round trip. Weights above VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES
(default: the memory-side cache size, read from the hardware once at first
use, 256 MiB on MI355X; see envs.py for what the cap controls and how to
tune it) therefore skip the skinny path at 1 < n <= 5 and fall through to
the generic GEMM.

n == 1 always keeps wvSplitK: the n=1 kernel variant shows no pathology on
large weights, and its fall-through would be a numerics change with no speed
win, so single-row calls stay on the stock path.

Returns True (keep wvSplitK) when n <= 1 or the weight is under the cap;
otherwise returns False after emitting a census WARNING (once per (shape, n)
per process) naming the redirected site.

      *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.maybe_pad_weight_avoid_cache_aliasing*
`maybe_pad_weight_avoid_cache_aliasing(weight)`

Offset a dense weight's row stride so it stops aliasing.

Returns a view with the original shape whose row stride is one cache line
wider, or `weight` unchanged when the pad does not apply.

                      *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.maybe_use_skinny_gemm*
`maybe_use_skinny_gemm(layer)`

Mark `layer` for the skinny GEMM if its weight shape has a plan.

         *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.warmup_rocm_skinny_gemm_workspaces*
`warmup_rocm_skinny_gemm_workspaces(device)` `cached`

Eagerly allocate wvSplitKrc's per-device split-K workspace pool.

wvSplitKrc partitions one per-device allocation into `kWvSlots` slots
(csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu) and hands each stream one on first
use, so that two streams never share the split-K partials and counters.

The pool is otherwise created lazily on the first qualifying GEMM
(csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu), which can be the first real request
--- after the KV cache backing buffer exists. If it landed in that segment's
rounding tail, it would pin the entire segment at engine shutdown; it could
also land inside a cudagraph capture, where it would be taken from the
graph's private pool and its zero-fill would become a replayed graph node.

                        *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.wvsplitkrc_dispatch*
`wvsplitkrc_dispatch(n, k, m, cu_count)`

Pick the K-shard split for wvSplitKrc and say whether the shape fits.

Mirrors wvSplitKrc() in csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu, which is also
where the shard cap is explained. Both must pick the same chunkk or the
workspace check here bounds the wrong k_rnd.

Returns: ~

- `int` -- The CHUNKK the kernel will dispatch with, and whether the CU
  budget and
- `bool` -- split-K workspace admit the shape at all.

  *vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding*
`VocabParallelEmbedding`

Bases: `PluggableLayer`

Embedding parallelized in the vocabulary dimension.

Adapted from torch.nn.Embedding, note that we pad the vocabulary size to
make sure it is divisible by the number of model parallel GPUs.

In order to support various loading methods, we ensure that LoRA-added
embeddings are always at the end of TP-sharded tensors. In other words, we
shard base embeddings and LoRA embeddings separately (both padded), and
place them in the same tensor. In this example, we will have the original
vocab size = 1010, added vocab size = 16 and padding to 64. Therefore, the
total vocab size with padding will be 1088 (because we first pad 1010 to
1024, add 16, and then pad to 1088). Therefore, the tensor format looks like
the following: TP1, rank 0 (no sharding): |< --------BASE-------- >|< -BASE
PADDING-- >|< -----LORA------ >|< -LORA PADDING-- >| corresponding token_id:
| 0 | 1 | ... | 1009 | -1 | ... | -1 | 1010 | ... | 1025 | -1 | ... | -1 |
index: | 0 | 1 | ... | 1009 | 1010 | ... | 1023 | 1024 | ... | 1039 | 1040 |
... | 1087 |

TP2, rank 0: |< --------------------BASE--------------------- >|<
-----LORA------ >|< -LORA PADDING- >| corresponding token_id: | 0 | 1 | 2 |
... | 497 | 498 | ... | 511 | 1010 | ... | 1025 | -1 | ... | -1 | index: | 0
| 1 | 2 | ... | 497 | 498 | ... | 511 | 512 | ... | 527 | 528 | ... | 543 |
TP2, rank 1: |< -----------BASE----------- >|< -BASE PADDING- >|<
-----------LORA PADDING----------- >| corresponding token_id: | 512 | 513 |
514 | ... | 1009 | -1 | ... | -1 | -1 | ... | -1 | -1 | ... | -1 | index: |
0 | 1 | 2 | ... | 497 | 498 | ... | 511 | 512 | ... | 527 | 528 | ... | 543
|

Parameters: ~

- `num_embeddings` (int) -- vocabulary size.
- `embedding_dim` (int) -- size of hidden state.
- `params_dtype` (dtype | None, default: None ) -- type of the parameters.
- `org_num_embeddings` (int | None, default: None ) -- original vocabulary
  size (without LoRA).
- `padding_size` (int, default: DEFAULT_VOCAB_PADDING_SIZE ) -- padding size
  for the vocabulary.
- `quant_config` (QuantizationConfig | None, default: None ) -- quant config
  for the layer
- `prefix` (str, default: '' ) -- full name of the layer in the state dict
- `disable_tp` (bool, default: False ) -- If true, tensor parallelism will
  be disabled for this layer.
- `reduce_results` (bool, default: True ) -- Whether to all-reduce
  contributions from vocabulary shards.
- `quant_method` (QuantizeMethodBase | None, default: None ) -- Preselected
  quantization method for model-specific layers.
- `parallel_group` (GroupCoordinator | None, default: None ) -- Process
  group used to shard and reduce the embedding.

Methods: ~

- `forward` -- Look up IDs, optionally reducing contributions from
  vocabulary shards.
- `get_sharded_to_full_mapping` -- Get a mapping that can be used to reindex
  the gathered

*vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding.get_sharded_to_full_mapping*
`get_sharded_to_full_mapping()`

Get a mapping that can be used to reindex the gathered logits for sampling.

During sampling, we gather logits from all ranks. The relationship of
index->token_id will follow the same format as outlined in the class
docstring. However, after the gather, we want to reindex the final logits
tensor to map index->token_id one-to-one (the index is always equal the
token_id it corresponds to). The indices returned by this method allow us to
do that.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch*

Apply dense or sparse weight updates in checkpoint coordinates.

The model's `load_weights` method still handles checkpoint-name mapping, TP
slicing, and packed parameters. Sparse patches use NaN to mark unchanged
checkpoint elements. The supported sparse-loader contract permits only final
same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_` writes. Composed, multi-stage, and
custom-write loaders are unsupported.

Classes: ~

- `CheckpointWeightPatch` -- Describe one dense or sparse
  checkpoint-coordinate update.

Functions: ~

- `load_checkpoint_weight_patches` -- Load ordered patches through the
  model's checkpoint loader.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch.CheckpointWeightPatch*
`CheckpointWeightPatch`

Bases: `NamedTuple`

Describe one dense or sparse checkpoint-coordinate update.

Attributes: ~

- `name` (str) -- Checkpoint weight name passed to the model loader.
- `shape` (tuple[int, ...]) -- Full checkpoint tensor shape.
- `dtype` (dtype) -- Checkpoint tensor dtype.
- `values` (Tensor) -- The flattened full tensor for a dense patch, or the
  values at indices for a sparse patch.
- `indices` (Tensor | None) -- Flat indices into the full checkpoint tensor
  described by shape. None makes values a dense replacement.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch._load_nan_masked_weights*
`_load_nan_masked_weights(model, weights)`

Load NaN-masked checkpoint tensors while preserving runtime values at NaNs.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch._validate_sparse_patches*
`_validate_sparse_patches(patches, max_chunk_bytes,
    validate_unique_indices)`

Check whole batches at once, since launching work per patch is slow.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch.load_checkpoint_weight_patches*
`load_checkpoint_weight_patches(model, patches, *,
    max_chunk_bytes=_DEFAULT_PATCH_CHUNK_BYTES, validate_unique_indices=True)`

Load ordered patches through the model's checkpoint loader.

A call may contain either dense or sparse patches, but not both. A repeated
name starts a new loader call, so patches for that weight are applied in
input order. A later patch may update positions changed by an earlier patch.
Each sparse patch creates a full checkpoint-shaped tensor whose NaNs mark
unchanged elements. Each locally applied sparse patch must use one final
same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_`. Intermediate or unrelated `copy_`
calls, composed loaders, and custom write paths are unsupported.
`max_chunk_bytes` is a batching target; one tensor may exceed it.

Online checkpoint-format dense updates require the caller to manage vLLM's
layerwise reload lifecycle. Sparse online updates modify initialized model
tensors in place and must not use that lifecycle. Patch shapes, dtypes,
value lengths, and sparse indices are validated before loading begins.

This function does not roll back a partial update. If a loader fails after a
write, some destinations may already be changed. Do not serve from the
affected worker until a known baseline has been restored or the worker has
been restarted.

Parameters: ~

- `model` (Module) -- Model whose native load_weights method applies the
  patches.
- `patches` (Iterable[CheckpointWeightPatch]) -- Dense replacements or
  sparse updates in checkpoint coordinates.
- `max_chunk_bytes` (int, default: _DEFAULT_PATCH_CHUNK_BYTES ) -- Target
  checkpoint tensor bytes per model.load_weights call and patch bytes per
  sparse validation batch. A single tensor may exceed this target.
- `validate_unique_indices` (bool, default: True ) -- Whether to reject
  duplicate sparse indices within each patch. Repeated patches may update
  the same positions. Disable only for a trusted producer that already
  guarantees unique positions within each patch.

Returns: ~

- `set[str]` -- Union of the weight names reported by all model.load_weights
  calls.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter*

Filter out non-local expert weights during loading to avoid redundant I/O.

In DP+EP deployments each rank only needs its own expert shard. Skipping
non-local expert tensors before they are read from disk eliminates the
majority of storage I/O for MoE models (experts typically account for ~85-90
% of total weight bytes).

Functions: ~

- `compute_eplb_local_expert_ids` -- Compute the logical expert ids ep_rank
  must load when EPLB is on.
- `compute_local_expert_ids` -- Compute the set of global expert ids owned
  by ep_rank.
- `parse_expert_id` -- Return the expert id embedded in weight_name, or None
  if it is
- `should_skip_weight` -- Return True if weight_name is an expert weight
  that does not

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.compute_eplb_local_expert_ids*
`compute_eplb_local_expert_ids(num_experts, num_redundant_experts, ep_size,
    ep_rank)`

Compute the logical expert ids ep_rank must load when EPLB is on.

EPLB splits `num_experts + num_redundant_experts` physical slots linearly
across ranks and fills each from the initial physical-to-logical map, so
redundant slots can need experts from other ranks' shards. Rebalancing later
moves weights GPU-to-GPU, so loading only has to satisfy the initial map.

Returns `None` when EP is not active (`ep_size <= 1`).

  *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.compute_local_expert_ids*
`compute_local_expert_ids(num_experts, ep_size, ep_rank,
    placement='linear')`

Compute the set of global expert ids owned by ep_rank.

Returns `None` when EP is not active (`ep_size <= 1`), meaning all experts
are local and no filtering should be performed.

The distribution logic mirrors
`vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.layer.determine_expert_map`.

Parameters: ~

- `num_experts` (int) -- Total number of experts in the layer.
- `ep_size` (int) -- Expert parallel world size.
- `ep_rank` (int) -- Rank whose local expert ids are computed.
- `placement` (str, default: 'linear' ) -- "linear" for contiguous
  assignment, "round_robin" for interleaved assignment.

           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.parse_expert_id*
`parse_expert_id(weight_name)`

Return the expert id embedded in weight_name, or `None` if it is not an
per-expert weight.

Returns `None` for dense weights (attention, layernorm, embedding), shared
experts, and 3D fused-expert tensors where all experts are stored in a
single tensor without a numeric expert id in the name.

        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.should_skip_weight*
`should_skip_weight(weight_name, local_expert_ids)`

Return `True` if weight_name is an expert weight that does not belong to the
local rank and should be skipped during loading.

`IpcModelLoader`             *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader*

Bases: `BaseModelLoader`

Zero-copy loads a model using the weight cache daemon's sharing backend.

The model is initialized on the meta device and every parameter/buffer is
replaced by the daemon's post-quantized tensor, so
process_weights_after_loading is skipped entirely. The engine shares the
daemon's GPU memory.

Extra config keys (via --model-loader-extra-config):

- socket_path: explicit daemon socket path. Defaults to a per-GPU path
  derived from the physical GPU uuid and the cache role (target/draft).
- socket_dir: directory containing the daemon sockets.
- fallback: fall back to disk loading when fetching state fails because the
  daemon is unavailable or the fingerprints mismatch (default: True).
- connect_timeout_s: socket connect timeout (default: 5.0).
- state_timeout_s: timeout for the weight-transfer request (default: 300.0).

The weights live in externally held backend allocations, so sleep mode
(CuMemAllocator weight offloading) must not be used with this loader. If the
daemon exits, the CUDA driver keeps the mapped weights alive until the
engine exits, so the engine keeps serving; the loader watches the daemon and
warns since a restarted daemon then holds a second copy of the weights on
the GPU.

           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader._rebuild_storages*
`_rebuild_storages(state)`

Rebuild manifest tensors from one imported buffer per storage.

               *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader._watch_daemon*
`_watch_daemon()`

Watch for the exit of the daemon serving the zero-copy weights.

The daemon holds the watch connection open for its lifetime, so the
connection closes exactly when that daemon instance exits; a daemon
restarted on the same socket does not mask the loss.

          *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader._with_startup_wait*
`_with_startup_wait(op)`

Retry op until the daemon answers or the state timeout elapses; the daemon
may still be loading the model when the engine starts.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload*

Layerwise weight reloading utilities for vLLM.

This module provides functionality to reload model weights layer-by-layer,
which is useful for weight updates without full model reconstruction.

Limitations: 1. Composition with CPU offloading has not been implemented 2.
Tied parameters will only reflect processing from one of the parent layers
(for example, only processing from embed_tokens will have an effect) 3. This
design assumes that the number of weights loaded from disk is the same as
the number of weights created at model init time. This is not true for quant
methods which (1) pad weights or (2) load qkv weights into the same
parameter. Both of these cases are non-issues for today's quant methods, but
future quantizations may cause reloading to fail

  on
- `direct` -- Direct weight reload (VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct, or auto where
  it applies).
- `geometry` -- Integer geometry of the load plan: one traced copy_ as a box
  of the
- `inplace` --
- `layerwise` --
- `lifecycle` -- Begin and complete a checkpoint-format weight update in the
  reload mode
- `meta` --
- `plan` -- Load plan: which part of each checkpoint tensor this rank needs,
  and where
- `sanitize` --
- `trace` -- Tracing a model's weight loaders on zero-storage checkpoint
  tensors.
- `utils` --

`get_boxes(name)` *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.LoadPlan.get_boxes*

Parts of the checkpoint tensor this rank needs; `None`: nothing.

For engines that send or read only those slices (sharded RDT, NCCL M2N
follow-ups); an engine that receives full tensors calls `load_planned`
instead.

`get_dest(name)`   *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.LoadPlan.get_dest*

(part of a box, live tensor) pairs: copying each part, reshaped to its
tensor's shape, into that tensor is exactly what the loader would have
written. `None`: fallback, send the full tensor through `load_weights`.
Write only between `start_reload` and `finish_reload`; never read. A tensor
may be in another dtype than the checkpoint tensor, so write it with
`copy_`, not as raw bytes.

`load_planned` copies full tensors through it; an engine that sends only
`get_boxes` copies its slices the same way.

                     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.check_plannable*
`check_plannable(model)`

Refuse a configuration no load plan supports: a reload mode other than
direct, EPLB, and online quantization (its loaders quantize what they load).
Reads only configuration, so an engine can call it before `start_reload`
changes the model. Direct reload's own refusals run in
`begin_direct_reload`.

Raises: ~

- `RuntimeError` -- the configuration cannot be planned.

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.finalize_layerwise_processing*
`finalize_layerwise_processing(model, model_config)`

Apply processing to any layers which were not layerwise processed during
loading. This includes attention layers and layers which have weight
elements which are not loaded (due to padding).

This function should be applied after `initialize_layerwise_reload` is
applied unwrap the layerwise weight loaders.

Parameters: ~

- `model` (Module) -- model to finalize processing for
- `model_config` (ModelConfig) -- config needed for applying processing to
  attention layers

                       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.finish_reload*
`finish_reload(model, model_config, device)`

Complete the weight update `start_reload` began.

         *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.initialize_layerwise_reload*
`initialize_layerwise_reload(model, *, defer_processing=False)`

Set up layerwise weight loading with deferred processing.

Must be called after `record_metadata_for_reloading`. This function: 1.
Saves current kernel tensors for later copying 2. Restores layer
parameters/buffers from metadata (on meta device) 3. Wraps weight loaders to
defer processing until all weights are loaded

When all weights for a layer are loaded, the wrapped loaders will: 1.
Materialize the layer onto the target device 2. Load all cached weights 3.
Run quantization processing if applicable 4. Copy processed values back to
original tensor storage

With defer_processing=True, only finalize_layerwise_reload triggers
processing.

                        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.load_planned*
`load_planned(model, plan, weights)`

Load full checkpoint tensors as `plan` says: copy each direct name's boxes
into its destinations, skip names this rank needs nothing of, and pass
fallbacks to `model.load_weights`. Call between `start_reload` and
`finish_reload`.

Copies are batched, so each tensor `weights` yields must stay unchanged
until this call returns: do not reuse one buffer across items.

                          *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.plan_loads*
`plan_loads(model, metadata)`

Trace `model.load_weights` over the declared checkpoint tensors once and
return where each lands on this rank.

Call between `start_reload` and `finish_reload`: the plan traces the real
tensors in the layout `begin_direct_reload` applied. Incoming tensors are
data-free traces, so nothing is loaded. Loaders' constant writes land, as on
the `load_weights` path; so do writes into non-checkpoint GPU tensors fed by
a read of a checkpoint tensor (a mirror), which are not restored: that name
falls back and the update rewrites them. Module, parameter and buffer state
a loader sets stays, as it would after `load_weights`.

Raises: ~

- `ValueError` -- a name is declared twice.
- `RuntimeError` -- the model cannot be planned.

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.record_metadata_for_reloading*
`record_metadata_for_reloading(model)`

Record layer metadata needed for later reloading.

Stores parameter and buffer metadata as meta tensors for restoration. Must
be called before `initialize_layerwise_reload`.

`start_reload(model)`   *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.start_reload*

Begin a weight update in the configured mode.

                *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.weight_update_active*
`weight_update_active()`

Whether a weight update is running, when one `load_weights` call may hold
only part of the checkpoint. Process-wide, so a module nested in the model
passed to `start_reload` sees it too.

          *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer.TensorizerConfig._keys*
`_keys` `class-attribute`

Configuration class for Tensorizer settings.

These settings configure the behavior of model serialization and
deserialization using Tensorizer.

Attributes: ~

- `tensorizer_uri` -- Path to serialized model tensors. Can be a local file
  path or a S3 URI. Unless a tensorizer_dir is passed to this object's
  initializer, this is a required argument.
- `tensorizer_dir` -- Path to a directory containing serialized model
  tensors, and all other potential model artifacts to load the model, such
  as configs and tokenizer files. Can be passed instead of tensorizer_uri
  where the model.tensors file will be assumed to be in this directory.
- `vllm_tensorized` -- If True, indicates that the serialized model is a
  vLLM model. This is used to determine the behavior of the
  TensorDeserializer when loading tensors from a serialized model. It is far
  faster to deserialize a vLLM model as it utilizes tensorizer's optimized
  GPU loading. Note that this is now deprecated, as serialized vLLM models
  are now automatically inferred as vLLM models.
- `verify_hash` -- If True, the hashes of each tensor will be verified
  against the hashes stored in the metadata. A HashMismatchError will be
  raised if any of the hashes do not match.
- `num_readers` -- Controls how many threads are allowed to read
  concurrently from the source file. Default is None, which will dynamically
  set the number of readers based on the number of available resources and
  model size. This greatly increases performance.
- `encryption_keyfile` -- File path to a binary file containing a binary key
  to use for decryption. None (the default) means no decryption. See the
  example script in examples/features/tensorize_vllm_model.py.
- `s3_access_key_id` -- The access key for the S3 bucket. Can also be set
  via the S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable.
- `s3_secret_access_key` -- The secret access key for the S3 bucket. Can
  also be set via the S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variable.
- `s3_endpoint` -- The endpoint for the S3 bucket. Can also be set via the
  S3_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon*

Weight cache daemon for fast engine restarts.

One daemon process per GPU holds the post-quantized, TP-sharded weights of
its rank in GPU memory and serves shared storage handles to vLLM engines
over a Unix domain socket. Restarting engines map the weights zero-copy
instead of reloading from disk.

Launch one daemon per TP rank with a single command:

>text
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 4
<
Engines then load from the daemons with:

>text
    vllm serve /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
        --load-format ipc_cache
<
Tensor, expert, data and pipeline parallelism are supported.

For multi-node tensor parallelism, run one launcher per node with a shared
rendezvous so the global TP group forms across nodes (weight sharing is
node-local, so each node serves only its local GPUs' shards). Reuse the same
`--nnodes`/`--node-rank`/`--master-addr` flags you pass the engine, plus a
`--weight-cache-master-port` distinct from the engine's `--master-port`:

>text
    # node 0 (8 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
        --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 --master-addr 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
    # node 1 (8 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
        --nnodes 2 --node-rank 1 --master-addr 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
<
The global TP rank of local GPU `i` on node `r` is
`r * (tp_size // nnodes) + i`, matching vLLM's contiguous per-node rank
assignment, so each engine worker maps its shard from the daemon on its own
node. With pipeline parallelism each node additionally runs one daemon per
PP stage; the global rank is `pp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank`.

For data parallelism (e.g. a TP1 x DP16 x EP decode fleet) run one launcher
per node with the engine's DP placement flags. Local GPU `i` serves DP rank
`start_rank + i // tp_size` and TP rank `i % tp_size`, and all
`dp_size * tp_size` daemons form one world group on
`--data-parallel-address`/`--weight-cache-master-port` so the expert shards
are laid out exactly as in the engine:

>text
    # node r (4 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
        --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 4 \
        --data-parallel-start-rank 4r --data-parallel-address 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
<
Data parallelism also combines with multi-node tensor parallelism: pass both
flag sets (`--nnodes`/`--node-rank`/`--master-addr` and the DP flags with a
reachable `--data-parallel-address`). Each node then serves a contiguous
block of the `dp_size * tp_size` global ranks, e.g. TP8 x DP2 on 4 nodes:

>text
    # node r (4 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
        --nnodes 4 --node-rank r --master-addr 10.0.0.1 \
        --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-address 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
<
With MTP, EAGLE or EAGLE3 speculative decoding the launcher additionally
starts a draft daemon group that caches the draft model. It uses its own
cache key, Unix sockets (`*_draft.sock`) and rendezvous port
(`--weight-cache-draft-master-port`, default
`--weight-cache-master-port + 1`), so each process serves exactly one model
role. Other draft types are not cached and keep loading from disk in the
engine. With pipeline parallelism only the draft daemons of the last stage
serve the draft model.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._acquire_gpu_lock*
`_acquire_gpu_lock(socket_path)`

Take an exclusive lock guarding this GPU's socket path.

The lock is advisory and released automatically when the daemon exits (or
crashes), so a stale socket is only ever removed by whoever owns the lock. A
running daemon holding it makes a second daemon fail fast instead of
clobbering the live socket.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._export_state*

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._handle_watch*

Zero-copy engines keep serving from the mapped weights after the daemon
exits; the closed connection tells them their daemon is gone.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon.get_model*
`get_model()`

Load the daemon's model, composed from the configured loader.

Runs the quantization check after model creation but before the slow weight
load, so an unsupported method fails fast. Online quantization always fails
the check, so load_model's finalize step for it is unnecessary here.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon.release_distributed*
`release_distributed()`

Release process groups and BLAS workspaces after loading and warmup.

Serving only exports shared storage handles, so the communicators (NCCL,
custom all-reduce and FlashInfer workspaces) and cached BLAS scratch would
otherwise pin GPU memory for the daemon's lifetime.

connection error (and fall back to disk) until the daemon is ready.

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.plan_local_ranks*
`plan_local_ranks(parallel_config)`

`(local_rank, dp_rank, pp_rank, tp_rank)` for every local daemon.

Global ranks enumerate DP, PP, then TP:
`global = dp_rank * pp_size * tp_size + pp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank`. With
`--nnodes` the engine hands each node a contiguous block of global ranks, so
node `r` serves `node_rank * local + i`; without it a launcher's block
starts at `--data-parallel-start-rank * tp_size`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader*

Map post-processed weights from a local daemon's pluggable sharing backend.

Classes: ~

- `IpcModelLoader` -- Zero-copy loads a model using the weight cache
  daemon's sharing backend.

     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader*
`IpcModelLoader`

Bases: `BaseModelLoader`

Zero-copy loads a model using the weight cache daemon's sharing backend.

The model is initialized on the meta device and every parameter/buffer is
replaced by the daemon's post-quantized tensor, so
process_weights_after_loading is skipped entirely. The engine shares the
daemon's GPU memory.

Extra config keys (via --model-loader-extra-config):

- socket_path: explicit daemon socket path. Defaults to a per-GPU path
  derived from the physical GPU uuid and the cache role (target/draft).
- socket_dir: directory containing the daemon sockets.
- fallback: fall back to disk loading when fetching state fails because the
  daemon is unavailable or the fingerprints mismatch (default: True).
- connect_timeout_s: socket connect timeout (default: 5.0).
- state_timeout_s: timeout for the weight-transfer request (default: 300.0).

The weights live in externally held backend allocations, so sleep mode
(CuMemAllocator weight offloading) must not be used with this loader. If the
daemon exits, the CUDA driver keeps the mapped weights alive until the
engine exits, so the engine keeps serving; the loader watches the daemon and
warns since a restarted daemon then holds a second copy of the weights on
the GPU.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader._rebuild_storages*
`_rebuild_storages(state)`

Rebuild manifest tensors from one imported buffer per storage.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader._watch_daemon*
`_watch_daemon()`

Watch for the exit of the daemon serving the zero-copy weights.

The daemon holds the watch connection open for its lifetime, so the
connection closes exactly when that daemon instance exits; a daemon
restarted on the same socket does not mask the loss.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader._with_startup_wait*
`_with_startup_wait(op)`

Retry op until the daemon answers or the state timeout elapses; the daemon
may still be loading the model when the engine starts.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                      *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.protocol*

WeightCacheKey fingerprinting and socket protocol for the weight cache
daemon.

The protocol uses pickle over a Unix domain socket and is only intended for
communication between trusted local processes owned by the same user. The
sockets live in a per-user private directory (mode 0700) and the daemon
restricts the socket file permissions to the owner (0600). Both the daemon
and the engine verify that the directory and socket are owned by the current
user and are not group/world accessible before trusting them, so a different
local user cannot pre-plant a malicious socket at a predictable path.

Classes: ~

- `CacheConfigMismatchError` -- Raised when the daemon's cached weights
  don't match the engine.
- `UnsupportedPlatformForIPCError` -- Raised when the current platform
  cannot share CUDA IPC handles.
- `UnsupportedQuantForIPCError` -- Raised when a quantization method is not
  verified for IPC weight sharing.
- `WeightCacheKey` -- Fingerprint of the cached weights.
- `WeightCacheState` -- Consumer-side DTO decoded from a daemon's get_state
  response.
- `WeightCacheUnavailableError` -- Raised when no weight cache daemon is
  reachable or usable.

Functions: ~

- `check_ipc_platform_support` -- Hard-error unless the current platform can
  share CUDA IPC handles.
- `check_ipc_quant_support` -- Hard-error unless every quant method supports
  pre-processed weights.
- `check_weight_cache_loader_support` -- Reject deployments a weight cache
  loader cannot serve (platform, EPLB, role).
- `ensure_private_socket_dir` -- Create the socket directory (if needed)
  locked down to the owner.
- `get_current_device_uuid` -- UUID of the physical GPU backing the current
  accelerator device.
- `get_socket_dir` -- Return the directory that holds the daemon sockets.
- `get_socket_path` -- Socket path of a daemon group; is_draft=False is the
  target.
- `hash_checkpoint` -- Fingerprint checkpoint content from local safetensors
  metadata.
- `hash_rope_parameters` -- Fingerprint the text RoPE parameters used to
  construct cached buffers.
- `parse_seed_address` -- Split a seed address into a Unix socket path or a
  (host, port).
- `recv_json` -- Receive one JSON message.
- `verify_peer_is_owner` -- Best-effort check that the connecting peer runs
  as the current user.
- `verify_private_dir` -- Verify a directory is a real dir owned by us and
  not world/group readable.
- `verify_socket_owner` -- Verify the socket lives in a private dir and is
  owned by the current user.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.transport*

Daemon-to-daemon seeding over authenticated JSON/TCP or local pickle.

A `Seedable` is one kind of state a daemon can seed to or from a peer
daemon, including warmup caches and weight shards. The target names what it
wants by kind and key fields; the source resolves the key to a payload; the
target validates and installs it:

>text
    request:  {"kind": "flashinfer_autotune", <key fields>..., "token": "..."}
    response: {"status": "ok", "payload": <kind-specific>}
              {"status": "miss"} | {"status": "error", "message": "..."}
<
Remote payloads are JSON values. Large binary state (weights) must not be
inlined: the payload then describes the transfer (e.g. a storage manifest),
and the caller drives the data plane itself.

The TCP connection is unencrypted beyond the shared token; keep the listener
on a trusted network.

Classes: ~

- `SeedConfig` -- A daemon's D2D endpoints and shared token (Unix paths need
  none).
- `SeedTransport` -- The daemon's D2D seeding endpoint: serves and fetches
  seedables.
- `Seedable` -- One kind of state that can flow between peer daemons, both
  ways.

          *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.transport.SeedConfig*
`SeedConfig`

Bases: `NamedTuple`

A daemon's D2D endpoints and shared token (Unix paths need none).

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.transport.SeedTransport*
`SeedTransport`

The daemon's D2D seeding endpoint: serves and fetches seedables.

Methods: ~

- `adopt` -- Best-effort: fetch and install seedable from the source daemon.
- `fetch` -- Fetch and validate a seed payload; None on a miss, else raise.
- `handle_request` -- Source side: answer one request; remote=True applies
  validate_remote.
- `request` -- Send one request to the source daemon; None with a log line
  on failure.
- `start_listener` -- Serve this rank's seedables to peers; None when
  unconfigured.

Attributes: ~

- (str | tuple[str, int] | None) -- The configured source daemon address, if
  any.

Any failure degrades to the local path with a log line.

  *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.build_weight_cache_key*
`build_weight_cache_key(vllm_config, model_config, *, is_draft=False)`

Fingerprint this rank's shard exactly as `WeightCacheDaemon` does.

Shared with the daemon so the peer loader requests the shard its own daemon
fingerprinted: TP/PP ranks come from the rank the daemon (or engine worker)
stamped on `parallel_config.rank`, and the DP placement follows the engine's
per-worker view. Draft models always use a single pipeline stage.

         *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.collect_tensors*
`collect_tensors(model)`

Collect a model's tensors, preserving tied-parameter aliases.

`named_parameters`/`named_buffers` are iterated with
`remove_duplicate=False` so tied weights (e.g. `lm_head.weight` sharing
storage with `embed_tokens.weight`) are not silently dropped. Each unique
tensor is kept once; every additional name that refers to the same tensor
object is recorded in the returned alias map so the client can re-establish
the shared identity instead of allocating uninitialized memory for it.

Returns: ~

- `dict[str, Tensor]` -- A (tensors, kinds, aliases) triple: tensors maps a
  canonical
- `dict[str, TensorKind]` -- name to its tensor, kinds maps it to "param" or
  "buffer", and
- `dict[str, str]` -- aliases maps each duplicate name to its canonical
  name.

   *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.exported_weight_bytes*
`exported_weight_bytes(storages)`

Allocation bytes of unique non-CPU storages mapped from cached state.

This is the memory the engine would otherwise allocate for the weights
itself. `memory_allocated()` also counts daemon-only state the engine never
maps (communication buffers, warmup workspaces, tensors outside
parameters/buffers that the engine rebuilds itself), so reporting it would
shrink the engine's KV cache below that of a disk load.

      *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.format_daemon_role*
`format_daemon_role(is_draft)`

Name of a daemon group: the target model or the draft.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.format_socket_role_suffix*
`format_socket_role_suffix(is_draft)`

Socket-name suffix keeping the draft group distinct from the target.

 *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.get_engine_dp_placement*
`get_engine_dp_placement(vllm_config, dp_rank)`

`(dp_size, dp_rank)` as the engine fingerprints this DP rank.

The engine runs the DP ranks of a non-MoE target as independent DP=1
replicas, so their workers all report `(1, 0)`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                               *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_tying*

Reconcile word embedding tying with what the checkpoint actually contains.

Functions: ~

- `maybe_retie_word_embeddings` -- Re-tie word embeddings that

           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_tying._get_untied_lm_head*
`_get_untied_lm_head(model)`

Locate an `lm_head` that could be tied to the input embeddings.

Returns `None` unless the model has exactly one of each, so that models with
several heads (such as MTP) or with already tied weights are left alone.
Both are found by type rather than by name, because `get_input_embeddings`
takes different arguments on multimodal models and the `lm_head` of a
multimodal model is nested inside its language model.

A quantized `lm_head` is also left alone. Its weights may be packed under
another name, and online quantization creates them after loading, so neither
their contents nor whether they were loaded can be established here. Note
that this is a property of the layer, not of the model: most quantized
models leave the `lm_head` and the input embeddings unquantized.

   *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_tying.maybe_retie_word_embeddings*
`maybe_retie_word_embeddings(model, model_config)`

Re-tie word embeddings that
|vllm.config.ModelConfig.maybe_untie_word_embeddings| untied, if the loaded
`lm_head` turned out to be identical to the input embeddings after all.

Checkpoints produced by quantization or fine-tuning tooling often keep a
redundant copy of the tied `lm_head`. Sharing the storage again reclaims the
memory it would otherwise cost.

Runs once per model: a direct reload reruns post-load processing on the
cold-started model and must keep its tying. Re-tying there would make
`lm_head` the input embeddings, and every later update's `lm_head` would be
dropped.

        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils._fill_random_fp8_codes*
`_fill_random_fp8_codes(param, generator)`

Fill an 8-bit float tensor with random finite codes across its range.

Real checkpoints scale FP8 weights to use the whole range, and the bit
activity of the operands sets GEMM power draw: values from a narrow range
(few exponent codes) let power-capped GPUs run measurably faster than real
weights do.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils.filter_mm_encoder_only_safetensors_files*
`filter_mm_encoder_only_safetensors_files(hf_weights_files, hf_folder,
    index_file, language_model_prefixes, *, weights_mapper=None)`

Drop safetensors shards that only contain language-model weights.

Used with `--mm-encoder-only` so Encoder-only EPD instances avoid reading
pure LM shards from disk/DRAM.

Each HF index key is classified by mapping through `weights_mapper` (when
provided) and testing the vLLM name against `language_model_prefixes`.
Without a mapper, HF names are compared directly (identity checkpoint
layout, e.g. Kimi `language_model.*`).

A shard is kept if it contains any non-LM key. Without an index file, or
when an LM module prefix is also the HF root of non-LM keys, returns
`hf_weights_files` unchanged: this fails closed so Molmo / Phi-4-MM / Muse
cannot under-load the encoder.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils.filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name*
`filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name(hf_weights_files,
    is_unused_weight)`

Drop safetensors shards in which `is_unused_weight` accepts every tensor.

Loaders that read whole files (InstantTensor, fastsafetensors, multi-thread,
eager, prefetch) cannot skip single tensors, so dropping shards is their
only way to avoid reading weights the model does not load.

Parameters: ~

- `hf_weights_files` (list[str]) -- Safetensors shard paths.
- `is_unused_weight` (Callable[[str], bool]) -- Returns True for checkpoint
  weight names the model does not load.

Returns: ~

- `list[str]` -- The shards holding at least one wanted tensor, or
  hf_weights_files
- `list[str]` -- unchanged when no shard does.

        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils.finalize_model_weights*
`finalize_model_weights(model, target_device=None)`

Run every module's own post-load hook after a full load or reload, each
after all of its submodules. Every load and update path finishes here.

Quantization methods and the submodules of quantized layers are skipped:
their quant method processes them, in the loader's per-layer pass.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils.initialize_single_dummy_weight*
`initialize_single_dummy_weight(param, low=None, high=None, seed=1234,
    name='')`

Fill `param` with deterministic dummy values suited to its dtype.

8-bit integer and packed FP4 params get random bytes (every FP4 code is
finite), except uint8 params named like a scale, which hold E8M0 scales and
get a fixed exponent. 8-bit float params get random finite codes across
their range, as real checkpoints use it, unless `low`/`high` are given.
Other integer params (e.g. indices) are left untouched. Other float params
are sampled from `[low, high]`, which defaults to +-1e-3.
